Why do you think there's something wrong with sum(l1)? That's
the right syntax in Stan and your model compiles.

Conceptually, you can increment. So if you set

loglike <- 0;

eather than setting entries of l1, you can just increment
loglike.

If you want to print a quantity, put it in
the transformed parameters block if it's used
in the model or in the generated quantities block if
it's not.

This may require you to move other definitions up,
but anything that is calculated as a local variable
in the model block can be calculated in the transformed
parameter block and saved.

If you're still having problems and need specifics, you'll
hae to send us an example.

You should define in transformed data if it only depends
on data, but those values don't get printed.

You should also read Andrew's notes to the list :-)

If you want to send the specific model and data that caused
the problem, just mail them to me as attachments (or to the
list as attachments with suffix .txt).

- Bob

> It doesn't work to declare something in the transformed parameters block and define it in the model block? If not, you

> could possibly move the pieces that you need to calculate the AIC or BIC with from model to transformed parameters.s

Nope -- variables can only be set in the block in
which they're defined.

But you can always move any computation you want to
save into transformed parameters itself, because
even in the model, everything must be defined in
terms of the parameters and data.

- Bob
